subject: VM closure play & scan calendar for SOC2 evidence

Subject: Request: scan cadence + CVE closure proof for SOC2 audit

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. Our SOC2 auditor asked us to provide a concise packet covering Redwood's vulnerability management rhythm for the last 12 months, specifically:

- monthly authenticated internal + external scans cadence (dates + tool used)
- SLA commitments for triage and remediation by severity (Critical/High/Medium) and proof of a sample closure
- evidence that CVE ownership is routed to engineers and tracked to closure (audit trail)

We need a short, exportable artifact by Friday (2026-10-09) to attach to the auditor portal. Can your security/sales team supply a compact file listing scheduled scans and a representative CVE closure log (redacted if needed)?

Also include any exception policy for legacy dependencies and how hotpatches are handled. If possible, point us to the Drive link or a single ZIP.

Appreciate it —
Anna

Anna —

Thanks for the note and the deadline. Looping in Laura (Security Ops) and Kimberly (Vuln Program) to assemble a compact packet. High-level plan below; we'll push a small Drive bundle and the two spreadsheets (scan calendar + CVE closure sample) by EOD Thursday so you have a day to review before Friday submission.

What we'll provide:
- scan-calendar-202610.csv: one-year scan schedule (internal authenticated, external unauthenticated, container images), tools listed (Trivy, Nessus, Qualys).
- cve-closure-log-202610.xlsx: representative CVE items (redacted hostnames), columns: CVE, severity, discovery-date, triage-owner, remediation-date, rollback-notes.
- a short narrative (1 page) describing SLA tiers: Critical = 48h response, mitigation plan within 7 days; High = 7/30; Medium = 30/90 (remediation windows vary by business impact).
- a screenshot of scan configuration and retention (screenshot-scan-config.png).

Laura/Kimberly — can you confirm the SLA wording and whether the auditor will accept the redacted closure rows as proof-of-remediation? Also flag any pending exceptions we should call out for Brightline.

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Anna Khoury <anna.khoury@brightline-fin.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:00:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: scan cadence + CVE closure proof for SOC2 audit

Hi all —

Attached is the pack I've prepared (Drive link in thread). Quick summary of what Brightline will see:

1) Scan rhythm and tooling
- Weekly authenticated internal scans (Nessus) on Tuesdays 02:00-05:00 PT (host-based + network), retained 13 months.
- Weekly external unauthenticated scans (Qualys) on Wednesdays 03:00-04:00 PT, retained 13 months.
- Daily CI/container image scans (Trivy) on merge to main with SBOM correlation; daily artifacts retained 90 days.
- Monthly penetration testing cadence (third-party) documented in the SOC2 binder; next scheduled 2027-01-12.

2) SLA and remediation windows (operational definition)
- Critical (RCE, active exploit): 1) Acknowledge and assign within 4 business hours; 2) Temporary mitigation (WAF rules, instance isolation) within 24-48 hours; 3) Code/patch remediation or validated workaround within 7 calendar days where feasible.
- High (privilege escalation, confidential data exposure): 1) Acknowledge within 8 business hours; 2) Remediation plan within 7 calendar days; 3) Complete fix or scheduled backlog remediation within 30 days depending on risk acceptance.
- Medium/Low: triage within 3 business days; remediation per release cadence (30-90 days).

3) Ownership and audit trail
- All findings create Jira tickets (SEC-####) and are routed to component owners via the CODEOWNERS mapping; ticket lifecycle records comments, commits, and PR references. The cve-closure-log includes sample Jira ids and commit SHAs for two closed Critical/High items (redacted hosts).

4) Exceptions and legacy dependency policy
- Exceptions are reviewed by Security Council and require a documented compensating control and a max exemption period of 90 days with quarterly re-approval. Legacy library exceptions are tracked in the dependency register (link included).

5) Hotpatching
- For Critical exploits, we run emergency patch windows (midnight patching allowed) and use out-of-band deployment with rollback playbooks. Evidence of an emergency hotpatch is the ticket, the deploy log, and the CVE closure entry.

Deliverables (links and small attachments):
- Drive bundle: https://drive.google.com/scan-pack/brightline-2026
- scan-calendar-202610.csv (attached)
- cve-closure-log-202610.xlsx (attached, hosts redacted)
- screenshot-scan-config.png (attached)

Anna — short ask: will the auditor require original host identifiers (FQDN/IP) in the proof? If they insist, we'll request a data-sharing agreement addendum and provide a secure ephemeral link with IPs masked except to the auditor.

Laura Bennett
Director, Security Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: scan-calendar-202610.csv, cve-closure-log-202610.xlsx, screenshot-scan-config.png

Thanks — confirming I've added two validated closure rows in the cve-closure-log sheet with the linked Jira tickets (SEC-2398, SEC-2411) and the PR/commit references. Both were remediated and verified in staging before production rollout; remediation notes are concise in the "status_notes" column.

A couple of operational clarifications for the auditor package:
- We include the initial scanner output (trimmed) plus the remediation PR link as proof.
- For Critical items we provide the mitigation timeline (time-to-detect, time-to-assign, time-to-remediate) — we've included exact timestamps for the two samples.
- If they request full hostnames, run it by legal/security; otherwise redacted evidence plus Jira/PR trace is accepted by most auditors.

I'll hand this off to Marcus to upload the Drive ZIP to your auditor portal, Anna. Marcus — I left a short README in the Drive bundle that explains each file.

Kimberly Park
